### Example 1

Informal statement:
For every natural number n, n + 0 = n.

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="induction">

</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="case">
Base case: when n is zero, 0 + 0 reduces to 0, so the two sides are equal.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="case">
Inductive case: suppose n + 0 = n. Then (suc n) + 0 reduces to suc (n + 0),
and rewriting with the induction hypothesis turns this into suc n.
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>

### Example 2

Informal statement:
For all natural numbers m and n, m + suc n = suc (m + n).

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):
+-suc : (m n : Nat) → m + suc n ≡ suc (m + n)

<INFORMAL_PROOF>
<STEP index="1" kind="induction">
We argue by induction on m, holding n fixed.
</STEP>
<STEP index="2" kind="case">
Base case: 0 + suc n reduces to suc n, and suc (0 + n) also reduces to suc n.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="case">
Inductive case: assume m + suc n = suc (m + n). Then (suc m) + suc n reduces
to suc (m + suc n), which by the induction hypothesis equals suc (suc (m + n)),
which is suc ((suc m) + n).
</STEP>
</INFORMAL_PROOF>

### Example 3

Informal statement:
Addition of natural numbers is commutative: m + n = n + m.

Formal statement (Agda, for reference only):

<STEP index="2" kind="lemma" name="plusSucRight">

</STEP>

</STEP>
<STEP index="4" kind="case">
Base case: 0 + n reduces to n, and n + 0 equals n by the first lemma.
</STEP>
<STEP index="5" kind="case">
Inductive case: assume m + n = n + m. Then suc m + n reduces to suc (m + n),

<STEP index="1" kind="step">
Setting. We work in a closed monoidal category with tensor product $\otimes$, internal hom $[A,B]$, and evaluation morphisms $\mathrm{ev}_{A,B} : [A,B] \otimes A \to B$. Let $\alpha_{P,Q,R} : (P \otimes Q) \otimes R \to P \otimes (Q \otimes R)$ be the associator. We use that $\alpha$ is natural in each of its three arguments, and that $\otimes$ of morphisms satisfies the interchange law. The unit isomorphisms do not occur in the argument.

<STEP index="2" kind="step">
Definitions. For objects $P, A, B$ and a morphism $q : P \otimes A \to B$, the universal property of the internal hom provides a morphism $\Lambda q : P \to [A,B]$ with $\mathrm{ev}_{A,B} \circ (\Lambda q \otimes \mathrm{id}_A) = q$. For $u : A' \to A$ and $v : B \to B'$ we define $[u,v] : [A,B] \to [A',B']$ to be $\Lambda(v \circ \mathrm{ev}_{A,B} \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes u))$. For objects $X, Y, Z$ we define $\gamma_{X,Y,Z} := \mathrm{ev}_{Y,Z} \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \mathrm{ev}_{X,Y}) \circ \alpha : ([Y,Z] \otimes [X,Y]) \otimes X \to Z$. We define $c_{X,Y,Z} : [Y,Z] \otimes [X,Y] \to [X,Z]$ to be $\Lambda \gamma_{X,Y,Z}$, taking $P = [Y,Z] \otimes [X,Y]$, $A = X$, $B = Z$. Finally, $L\,X\,Y\,Z : [Y,Z] \to [[X,Y],[X,Z]]$ is the morphism $\Lambda c_{X,Y,Z}$ taken with respect to the factor $[X,Y]$, so that $\mathrm{ev}_{[X,Y],[X,Z]} \circ (L\,X\,Y\,Z \otimes \mathrm{id}_{[X,Y]}) = c_{X,Y,Z}$.
</STEP>
<STEP index="3" kind="lemma" name="transpose_uniqueness">
For objects $P, A, B$, if $h, k : P \to [A,B]$ satisfy $\mathrm{ev}_{A,B} \circ (h \otimes \mathrm{id}_A) = \mathrm{ev}_{A,B} \circ (k \otimes \mathrm{id}_A)$, then $h = k$.
</STEP>
<STEP index="4" kind="case">
Proof of transpose_uniqueness. Both $h$ and $k$ are morphisms $P \to [A,B]$ whose transposes $\mathrm{ev}_{A,B} \circ (- \otimes \mathrm{id}_A)$ are equal. The universal property of $[A,B]$ says that the transpose map from morphisms $P \to [A,B]$ to morphisms $P \otimes A \to B$ is injective, so $h = k$.
</STEP>
<STEP index="5" kind="lemma" name="ev_naturality">
For $u : A' \to A$ and $v : B \to B'$, we have $\mathrm{ev}_{A',B'} \circ ([u,v] \otimes \mathrm{id}_{A'}) = v \circ \mathrm{ev}_{A,B} \circ (\mathrm{id}_{[A,B]} \otimes u)$.
</STEP>
<STEP index="6" kind="case">
Proof of ev_naturality. Put $q := v \circ \mathrm{ev}_{A,B} \circ (\mathrm{id}_{[A,B]} \otimes u) : [A,B] \otimes A' \to B'$. By definition $[u,v] = \Lambda q$, and by the defining property of $\Lambda$ we have $\mathrm{ev}_{A',B'} \circ (\Lambda q \otimes \mathrm{id}_{A'}) = q$, which is the claim.
</STEP>
<STEP index="7" kind="lemma" name="special_evs">
Let $f : Y' \to Y$ and $g : Z \to Z'$. Then the following three identities hold. (i) $\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y} \circ ([\mathrm{id},f] \otimes \mathrm{id}_X) = f \circ \mathrm{ev}_{X,Y'}$, where $[\mathrm{id},f] : [X,Y'] \to [X,Y]$. (ii) $\mathrm{ev}_{X,Z'} \circ ([\mathrm{id},g] \otimes \mathrm{id}_X) = g \circ \mathrm{ev}_{X,Z}$, where $[\mathrm{id},g] : [X,Z] \to [X,Z']$. (iii) $\mathrm{ev}_{Y',Z'} \circ ([f,g] \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y'}) = g \circ \mathrm{ev}_{Y,Z} \circ (\mathrm{id}_{[Y,Z]} \otimes f)$.
</STEP>
<STEP index="8" kind="case">
Proof of special_evs. Identity (i) is ev_naturality with $u = \mathrm{id}_X$ and $v = f$, applied to the pair $A = X$, $B = Y'$, $A' = X$, $B' = Y$; the composite $\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y'} \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \mathrm{id}_X)$ is just $\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y'}$. </STEP>
<STEP index="10" kind="case">

<STEP index="11" kind="case">
By naturality of $\alpha$ in its first argument, $\alpha_{[Y',Z'],[X,Y'],X} \circ (([f,g] \otimes \mathrm{id}) \otimes \mathrm{id}_X) = ([f,g] \otimes \mathrm{id}_{[X,Y'] \otimes X}) \circ \alpha_{[Y,Z],[X,Y'],X}$. <STEP index="12" kind="case">

<STEP index="13" kind="case">
By special_evs (iii), $\mathrm{ev}_{Y',Z'} \circ ([f,g] \otimes \mathrm{id}_{Y'}) = g \circ \mathrm{ev}_{Y,Z} \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes f)$. Substituting, the left side equals $g \circ \mathrm{ev}_{Y,Z} \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes (f \circ \mathrm{ev}_{X,Y'})) \circ \alpha_{[Y,Z],[X,Y'],X}$, which is the right side.
</STEP>
<STEP index="14" kind="lemma" name="rhs_uncurried">
$\mathrm{ev}_{X,Z'} \circ \big( ([\mathrm{id},g] \circ c_{X,Y,Z} \circ (\mathrm{id}_{[Y,Z]} \otimes [\mathrm{id},f])) \otimes \mathrm{id}_X \big) = g \circ \mathrm{ev}_{Y,Z} \circ (\mathrm{id}_{[Y,Z]} \otimes (f \circ \mathrm{ev}_{X,Y'})) \circ \alpha_{[Y,Z],[X,Y'],X}$.
</STEP>
<STEP index="15" kind="case">
Proof of rhs_uncurried. By functoriality of $\otimes$, the left side equals $\mathrm{ev}_{X,Z'} \circ ([\mathrm{id},g] \otimes \mathrm{id}_X) \circ (c_{X,Y,Z} \otimes \mathrm{id}_X) \circ ((\mathrm{id} \otimes [\mathrm{id},f]) \otimes \mathrm{id}_X)$. </STEP>
<STEP index="16" kind="case">
Since $\mathrm{ev}_{X,Z} \circ (c_{X,Y,Z} \otimes \mathrm{id}_X) = \gamma_{X,Y,Z}$, the expression equals $g \circ \mathrm{ev}_{Y,Z} \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \mathrm{ev}_{X,Y}) \circ \alpha_{[Y,Z],[X,Y],X} \circ ((\mathrm{id} \otimes [\mathrm{id},f]) \otimes \mathrm{id}_X)$.

<STEP index="17" kind="case">
By naturality of $\alpha$ in its second argument, $\alpha_{[Y,Z],[X,Y],X} \circ ((\mathrm{id} \otimes [\mathrm{id},f]) \otimes \mathrm{id}_X) = (\mathrm{id} \otimes ([\mathrm{id},f] \otimes \mathrm{id}_X)) \circ \alpha_{[Y,Z],[X,Y'],X}$. <STEP index="18" kind="case">
By special_evs (i), $\mathrm{ev}_{X,Y} \circ ([\mathrm{id},f] \otimes \mathrm{id}_X) = f \circ \mathrm{ev}_{X,Y'}$. Substituting gives $g \circ \mathrm{ev}_{Y,Z} \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes (f \circ \mathrm{ev}_{X,Y'})) \circ \alpha_{[Y,Z],[X,Y'],X}$, which is the right side.
</STEP>
<STEP index="19" kind="lemma" name="composition_naturality">
As morphisms $[Y,Z] \otimes [X,Y'] \to [X,Z']$, we have $c_{X,Y',Z'} \circ ([f,g] \otimes \mathrm{id}_{[X,Y']}) = [\mathrm{id},g] \circ c_{X,Y,Z} \circ (\mathrm{id}_{[Y,Z]} \otimes [\mathrm{id},f])$.

<STEP index="20" kind="case">
Proof of composition_naturality. Let $S$ and $T$ denote the left and right sides. As morphisms $[Y,Z] \to [[X,Y'],[X,Z']]$, the transposes satisfy $\mathrm{ev}_{[X,Y'],[X,Z']} \circ ((L\,X\,Y'\,Z' \circ [f,g]) \otimes \mathrm{id}_{[X,Y']}) = c_{X,Y',Z'} \circ ([f,g] \otimes \mathrm{id}_{[X,Y']})$ and $\mathrm{ev}_{[X,Y'],[X,Z']} \circ (([[\mathrm{id},f],[\mathrm{id},g]] \circ L\,X\,Y\,Z) \otimes \mathrm{id}_{[X,Y']}) = [\mathrm{id},g] \circ c_{X,Y,Z} \circ (\mathrm{id}_{[Y,Z]} \otimes [\mathrm{id},f])$.

<STEP index="22" kind="case">

<STEP index="23" kind="lemma" name="L_naturality">
$L\,X\,Y'\,Z' \circ [f,g] = [[\mathrm{id},f],[\mathrm{id},g]] \circ L\,X\,Y\,Z$ as morphisms $[Y,Z] \to [[X,Y'],[X,Z']]$.
</STEP>
<STEP index="24" kind="case">
Proof of L_naturality. Let $M_1$ and $M_2$ denote the left and right sides. By transposed_sides, the transposes $\mathrm{ev}_{[X,Y'],[X,Z']} \circ (M_i \otimes \mathrm{id}_{[X,Y']})$ for $i = 1,2$ are equal to $c_{X,Y',Z'} \circ ([f,g] \otimes \mathrm{id})$ and $[\mathrm{id},g] \circ c_{X,Y,Z} \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes [\mathrm{id},f])$ respectively, and these are equal by composition_naturality. Applying transpose_uniqueness with $P = [Y,Z]$, $A = [X,Y']$, $B = [X,Z']$ gives $M_1 = M_2$.
</STEP>
